attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, introduced with 'I must repeat'. Not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: Unhedged 'will have spent' makes this a scored forecast. The start date 'since 2023' is reasonably drawn from the same post's earlier 'upwards of $200 billion... since 2023'. The threshold, 'over $200B', and the end-2025 horizon are preserved. The metric and the calendar-or-fiscal year basis are left unspecified, as in the source.

contract.note: The criteria do not impose a reading he did not give. They defer to 'the measure and year basis he meant', which he never stated, so the contract is hard to operationalise. Fiscal versus calendar years, and including or excluding finance leases, could move the total. The result therefore depends on an interpretation the speaker did not supply.

output.rationale: The end-2025 deadline has passed by the evaluation date, so the forecast is due for scoring. However, the packet contains no evidence items: the drafter collected no Microsoft capex figures and the one source considered was not used. Nothing in the packet shows cumulative 2023–2025 capex on any measure or year basis. Under the policy, facts I may remember cannot be imported, so the outcome is unresolved.
